thread.title: Dow stages U-turn into negative territory as Apple’s stock gives up $200 billion since peak

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Dow stages U-turn into negative territory as Apple’s stock gives up $200 billion since peak
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gave up a more than 200-point opening gain early Wednesday and turned negative, as shares of Apple Inc.
 AAPL, -2.73%
 slumped. The Dow
 DJIA, -0.90%
 had opened the session with an advance of as many as 214 points but was most recently down about 190 points, or 0.8%, at 25,095. The index is attempting to avoid a four-session skid, which would represent its longest string of declines since Aug. 13, according to FactSet data. Shares of Apple
 AAPL, -2.73%
 were down 2.6%, or $5.01, to $187.16 on Wednesday and are down 19.3% since hitting a peak in early October. A 20% drop would meet the traditional Wall Street definition of a bear market for Apple. Since that October peak, which took Apple to a value over $1 trillion, the Cupertino, Calif-based tech giant has given up $210 billion in value to $892.6 billion, according to FactSet data. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 index
 SPX, -0.84%
 was down 0.8% at 2,700, while the Nasdaq Composite Index
 COMP, -0.83%
 was down 0.8% at 7,143. Apple’s market value and its share price make it a significant catalyst for the market-cap weighted S&P 500 and Nasdaq and the price-weighted Dow.
